notes.read: A leaf-covered path runs back between white birch trunks into a misty autumn wood, dark firs on the right, the low sun glowing at the upper left. The lesson is about depth through mist: soft far trunks and firs first, a warm floor and path, golden leaf masses, then the big front birches with their dark bark marks and light last.
notes.order: Back to front: the misty sky and sun, the far trunks, firs and middle trunks, the floor and path, the leaves, the rock, then the front birches and the last lights. Planned by the v3 plan writer in a fresh context.

stages.name: Blend the misty sky over the whole canvas
steps: Inside the outlined area. It reaches all four edges of the canvas.
Paints: Pale gold for the glow, Misty blue across the rest, and Blue-violet mist for the soft upright streaks, as the after picture shows.
Mix enough Pale gold for this step and steps 11 and 20; cover it between them.
Mix enough Blue-violet mist for this step and steps 3 and 6; cover it between them.
Mix enough Misty blue for this step and step 4; cover it between them.
Brush: 1 1/2 inch flat. Load: Creamy paint. An even coat.
Start with Pale gold at the glow. Without rinsing, work Misty blue out from it, stroking back over the join. Then drag in upright Blue-violet mist streaks.
It should leave a soft, even haze, with gentle joins where two wet colors meet.
Watch out: Blending after the paint has started to drag. Acrylic sets in minutes, and scrubbing setting paint lifts it and leaves streaks. Fix: stop as soon as it drags.
Let it dry, then blend a new thin layer on top.

Brush: fan brush. Load: Thin paint. Stroke the brush on the palette until the bristles fan out.
Stamp only the tips, using the middle of the fan, not the side bristles. For a shape that widens, work from the top down in a zigzag and press harder as you go down.

technique_picks.technique_why: A misty autumn wood is a classic back-to-front paint-along: a blended haze, simple far trees, dabbed leaves, then bold birch trunks painted last over everything.

parts.name: The misty sky
parts.why: The background is one soft haze from gold by the sun to blue-violet on the right, blended wet in one go.

parts.name: The sun
parts.why: A small soft glowing disk in one pale color, painted in one move.

parts.name: The misty far trunks
parts.why: Far trunks in a wood, pulled thin and pale in the haze with no texture.
parts.left_out: The light side on the far trunks; at that distance they stay one soft pale color.

parts.name: The fir trees
parts.why: Dark firs on the right and hazy ones in the middle, stamped with a fan brush.

parts.name: The middle trunks
parts.why: A few nearer trunks by the far end of the path, pulled thick to thin, darker than the misty ones.
parts.left_out: Bark marks and branches on the middle trunks; they stay plain so the front birches stand out.

parts.name: The forest floor
parts.why: The ground is a flat base laid in horizontal strokes, lighter at the back and darker in front; the leaves go over it. Field-grass is the closest element, and its grass texture is replaced by the fallen leaves.

parts.name: The path
parts.why: Closest element: one dirt track pulled toward a single point in the mist, wide in front and thin at the back. It lacks a curve, so the path just bends gently as it narrows.

parts.name: The autumn leaves
parts.why: Masses of autumn leaves in the treetops, dabbed dark, then mid, then a few light.

parts.name: The mossy rock
parts.why: A low boulder with a lit top and a shaded underside, built from simple rounded pieces.

parts.name: The rock's shadow and light

parts.name: The front birch trunks
parts.why: White birch trunks with dark bark marks, shaded on the side away from the sun and lit on the sunny side.

parts.name: The birches' shading and bark patches

parts.name: The thin bark lines

parts.name: The sunlit leaves on the ground
